measures: CFS bandwidth throttling of ONE libx265 encode, taken from the cgroup's own cpu.stat around the encode, with libx265 at its own host-sized default parallelism (before) and at the pool size and frame-thread count derived from the cgroup CPU quota (after)
how_to_read: A figure here means something only against the figure beside it, taken the same way on the same machine. It is NEVER a build gate: an absolute threshold on a shared runner false-positives at roughly 45% (performance PB5), so a regression is argued by re-running the same encode and comparing to these numbers, not by a check that reds. The CFS counters are cgroup-wide, so they include anything else that ran in this container's cgroup during the encode; idle_window is the same counters with nothing encoding, and sizes that noise.

machine.cgroup: v2; the process sits at 0::/ of its own namespace, so the limit is the one at /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max
machine.note: a shared container carrying a real, finite CPU bandwidth limit: 5 CPUs of a 56-CPU host. The counters below are non-zero on both arms, so this is not a pair taken where they are always zero.

build.ffmpeg: N-125875-g5d4d3bdc61 linux64-gpl, the Dockerfile's FFMPEG_VERSION pin as installed by scripts/install-ffmpeg.sh

commit_note: the commit the measurement was taken AT, an ancestor of the commit carrying this file. The before arm is the argv the builder emits at 5c10f15 (origin/main before this change), which is the same argv with no parallelism in -x265-params. holdfast's own rules forbid dates in its files, and the commit identifies the tree more exactly than a date does.

encode.source: lavfi testsrc2=duration=5:size=1920x1080:rate=24, written as libx264 ultrafast at 20 Mb/s yuv420p (120 frames)
encode.knobs: the shipped defaults: encoder cpu, preset slow, crf 22, pixel_format auto (yuv420p10le for this 8-bit source)
encode.argv: ffmpeg -hide_banner -nostdin -loglevel error -y -i <source> -map 0 -map -0:d? -c copy -c:v libx265 -pix_fmt yuv420p10le -fps_mode passthrough -preset slow -crf 22 -x265-params <x265_params> -- <out>
encode.after_derived_by: engine.DeriveX265(0, "") on this machine: source cgroup, 5 whole CPUs from cpu.max
encode.method: the two arms interleaved, alternating which goes first, 3 seconds apart; each sample is the difference of /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.stat read immediately before and after one encode

after_against_before: Against the stored before-figure, taken the same way on this machine in the same session: throttled periods fell from a median of 194 of 218 (88.8%, range 85.2-90.0%) to 65 of 211 (32.7%, range 6.4-35.5%), and time spent throttled from a median of 53.5 s per encode (range 47.9-57.7 s) to 1.4 s (range 0.1-1.8 s); the two ranges do not overlap on either counter. Wall time moved from a median of 21.78 s to 21.11 s and CPU consumed from 104.8 to 98.0 CPU-seconds, but both ranges overlap (21.12-22.88 against 19.57-23.38 s; 102.5-109.8 against 91.2-103.6 CPU-s), so this record claims the throttling drop and not a speed-up. libx265 at its default built a 56-thread pool and 5 frame threads here, against 5 and 2 after.

vmaf_ac11.knobs: libx265 crf 22, preset slow, yuv420p10le; scored by internal/vmaf Score with vmaf_v0.6.1, subsample 1, 1 thread, comparison format yuv420p10le
vmaf_ac11.spread_across_runs: 0 on every score of every candidate: the three runs produced identical figures
vmaf_ac11.note: the three candidates are different files (195200, 195554 and 195541 bytes); the derived and host-default ones score the same to four places. The closest any score comes to its floor is chroma at 43.80 against 30.
